newsitem.title: EGYPT: Peace summit depends on end of sanctions - Egypt.
newsitem.headline: Peace summit depends on end of sanctions - Egypt.

text.p: An Egyptian government newspaper said on Thursday Israel must lift sanctions against Palestinians before the leaders of Egypt, Israel and the Palestinians could hold a summit to ease the latest Middle East peace crisis.
Israel suspended a resumption of its talks with the Palestinians and sealed off the West Bank and Gaza Strip after a twin suicide bombing in a crowded west Jerusalem market last week.

"An invitation from President Hosni Mubarak for a summit between himself, (Palestinian) President Yasser Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu must be preceded by specific arrangements," the daily al-Ahram said.

"Firstly, lifting the sanctions imposed by Israel against the Palestinian people because continued punishment of the Palestinians and leaving them without food and medicine will have dire consequences and no one will be able to control the results of a hunger revolution.

"Secondly, determining the general lines needed to activate the peace process so as to remove all obstacles that led to its freeze and deterioration so that we can rebuild confidence between Palestinians and Israel which will lead to the continuation of the peace process," al-Ahram added.
The double suicide bombing killed 15 people, including the two bombers.

Arafat was quoted by an Israeli newspaper on Thursday as saying measures imposed by Israel against the Palestinians since the explosions amounted to a declaration of war, and warned that he was preparing accordingly.
Egypt, which in 1979 became the first Arab state to sign a peace deal with Israel, considers itself an unofficial mediator in peace talks between Israel and its Arab neighbours.
Jordan's Crown Prince Hassan arrived in Egypt on Thursday for talks with Mubarak on ways to ease the latest crisis in Middle East peace efforts.
Prince Hassan proved unable in talks with Netanyahu in Jerusalem on Wednesday to persuade Israel to ease the sanctions imposed after the bombings.

Al-Ahram said once the two conditions for a summit were met, "it will be possible to persuade the Palestinians of the need for the meeting, its seriousness, effectiveness and worthiness in moving the peace process forward".
